topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, course context, and primary learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Genetic, environmental, and epidemiological determinants of cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental origins of cancer by comparing the roles of intrinsic cellular processes, genetic predisposition, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and mechanisms of oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological agents such as bacteria, parasites, and oncogenic viruses contribute to cancer development, highlighted by the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens, metabolic activation, and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which radiation and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation to form DNA adducts and induce mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, the two-stage carcinogenesis model, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of tumorigenesis, focusing on the distinction between initiators and promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental tissue susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies and considerations for identifying and evaluating carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the experimental, epidemiological, and genomic approaches used to detect mutagenic exposure, evaluate carcinogenicity, and weigh risks against benefits.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecturer's concluding wrap-up of the main themes and closing remarks.
